To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Up-regulation of GAP 43 (neuronal growth associated protein) and synapsin (presynaptic vesicle protein) in the hippocampus is correlated with the severity of the learning deficit in the Morris water maze task in the 3xTg-AD mouse model.
the up-regulation of GAP43 mRNA in the spinal cord of rats with peripheral nerve injury is mediated by the transcriptional activity of NF-κB.

the GAP-43 mRNA and protein are up-regulated in the hippocampus of the rat brain following a single session of contextual fear conditioning, and this up-regulation is associated with the acquisition of the fear memory.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role that the extracellular matrix plays in regulating the development of the CNS.
the role of the cytoskeleton and its regulatory proteins in the regulation of neuronal plasticity.
the role of GAP-43 in the regulation of axon growth and the development of synaptic connections, and with the mechanisms by which GAP-43 is involved.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression pattern of the GAP-43 protein is not altered by the presence or absence of the GAP-42 protein in the brain.
the up-regulation of GAP43 mRNA in the spinal cord is not a direct effect of the nerve lesion but rather an indirect consequence of the increased motor activity.

the present results suggest that the GAP-43 protein is involved in the regulation of the axon growth and that its expression is up-regulated in the axons during the regeneration of the injured spinal cord.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the up-regulation of GAP 43 is not sufficient to promote neurite outgrowth.
we have shown that the GAP-43 gene is up-regulated in the hippocampus and the cortex in response to a wide variety of stimuli, including stress, exercise, and environmental enrichment.

GAP-43 expression in neurons is regulated at the transcriptional level, which is controlled by a complex network of transcription factors, and that the expression of GAP-43 is also controlled by the phosphorylation of its promoter region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of a GAP-43 promoter-driven transgene can be used to drive the differentiation of neural stem cells into neurons and that these neurons can be used to repair a damaged brain.

the expression of GAP-43 and the expression of the genes that encode GAP-43, are up-regulated during the development of a variety of cancers, and that this up-regulation is correlated with the aggressiveness of these cancers.
